item.description:
Genre: Rock, Stage & Screen

Year: 2026
Video Source: YouTube
Audio Source: Qobuz

Often given the full title of "Leave Her Johnny, Leave Her", this is a traditional sea shanty turned ubiquitous folk song. Starting as a windlass or capstan shanty, the earliest known evidence of this song is found in W.B. Whall's autobiography School and Sea Days (1901), which places it in the 1860s. It was traditionally saved for the last day of a voyage, after which all crew would disembark the ship. The song would not be sung on naval ships, instead only on Private or Pirate ships, as the lyrics were often re-written to mock the Captain, Quartermaster, and other senior members of the crew. In navies, the disrespect of senior officers and crew would usually end in punishment. The song remains widely known, with covers from several popular folk artists, and was featured in the video game Assassin's Creed: Black Flag.

The ‘Her’ in the song’s title refers to the ship which the crew was manning, as Ships are traditionally referred to with feminine pronouns in Western, English speaking cultures. The ‘Johnny’ spoke of in the title is merely a general, “John Doe” style name for men commonly used in sea songs.

Black Flag’s viral and fan-favourite sea shanty has been re-recorded by Woodkid for the remake, Black Flag Resynced.
It’s not the first time Woodkid has been involved with Assassin’s Creed. His debut solo single ‘Iron’ featured in the trailer for Assassin’s Creed 3: Revelations. “The world of Assassin’s Creed has been very important to me and is very linked to my career,” he said in a statement. “I know Assassin’s Creed: Black Flag is a major episode for the audience. It’s a game about escapism, rebellion, and exploration. These are themes that are very important for my work. I’m very excited about what we’ve done.”
